language.name: English
module.temp-clean.name: Temp cleanup
module.temp-clean.desc: Scans and empties the temporary folders of the system and of apps.
module.big-files.name: Large file finder
module.big-files.desc: Searches the disk and sorts files from largest to smallest.
module.duplicates.name: Duplicate finder
module.duplicates.desc: Finds identical files by their SHA-256 checksums.
module.shredder.name: File shredder
module.shredder.desc: Deletes data beyond recovery by overwriting it several times.
module.metadata.name: Metadata remover
module.metadata.desc: Strips hidden information (location, author) from photos and documents.
module.xcode-cache.name: Xcode cleanup
module.xcode-cache.desc: Removes the temporary DerivedData files Xcode leaves behind.
module.macos-slim.name: macOS slimming
module.macos-slim.desc: Copies of opened attachments, previews and caches of Mail and Messages — mailboxes and conversations stay untouched.
module.pkg-cache.name: Linux package cache
module.pkg-cache.desc: Clears the cache and orphaned packages of the system's package manager (apt, pacman, dnf, zypper) and old snap revisions.
module.pkg-cache.desc.family: Clears the {family} cache and orphaned packages, and old snap revisions.
module.journald-trim.name: systemd log trimming
module.journald-trim.desc: Trims the journalctl logs to a chosen size or age.
module.journald-trim.desc.no-systemd: This system does not run systemd, so there is no journald log to trim.
module.disk-map.name: Disk map
module.disk-map.desc: Shows what takes up the disk as proportional tiles.
module.autostart.name: Startup manager
module.autostart.desc: Shows and turns off programs that start with the system.
module.health-monitor.name: Health monitor
module.health-monitor.desc: Live CPU and RAM, cache clearing and disk S.M.A.R.T. readings.
module.winsxs.name: WinSxS cleanup
module.winsxs.desc: Works with DISM to remove old file versions left by Windows Update.
module.services.name: Service manager
module.services.desc: Windows services in ready-made profiles (telemetry, Xbox, printing, maps) instead of a list of hundreds.
module.bloatware.name: Bloatware removal
module.bloatware.desc: Removes Store apps from this account, with the preinstalled ones marked, after a restore point.
module.time-machine.name: Time Machine
module.time-machine.desc: Removes local Time Machine snapshots with tmutil.
module.kernel-mgr.name: Kernel versions
module.kernel-mgr.desc: Lists and removes old kernels from /boot; the running one is locked.
module.desktop-theme.name: Desktop look
module.desktop-theme.desc: GTK themes, icons, cursors and interface fonts for GNOME and KDE Plasma; installs a theme or font from a folder.
module.desktop-theme.desc.desktop: {desktop} themes, icons, cursors and fonts; installs a theme or font from a folder.
module.desktop-theme.desc.unsupported: {desktop}: changing the look works in GNOME, KDE Plasma, Cinnamon, MATE, Xfce, Budgie and Pantheon; installing themes and fonts works everywhere.
module.grub-editor.name: Visual GRUB editor
module.grub-editor.desc: Menu timeout and default system in GRUB, Limine, systemd-boot or rEFInd; GRUB themes.
module.grub-editor.desc.loader: Default system and menu timeout in the {loader} configuration, with a backup before every change.
module.grub-editor.desc.unsupported: This system boots with {loader}; the editor supports GRUB, Limine, systemd-boot and rEFInd.
module.browser-hygiene.name: Browser hygiene
module.browser-hygiene.desc: Clears cache, cookies and history; compacts the browsers' SQLite databases.
module.vault.name: Password manager (Vault)
module.vault.desc: A local, encrypted store of logins and passwords, with a security audit.
module.winget-ui.name: Winget
module.winget-ui.desc: Apps with an update available, updated through the system's winget.
module.uninstaller.name: Uninstaller
module.uninstaller.desc: Lists installed apps (system package manager, flatpak, snap), uninstalls them and finds the config, cache and data a removed program left behind.
module.uninstaller.desc.family: Lists installed apps ({family}, flatpak, snap), uninstalls them and finds the config, cache and data a removed program left behind.
settings.access.desc: Full asks for every permission up front and remembers it. Selective grants permissions for one session and asks again after a restart.
settings.disk-access.granted.desc: Granted — modules also see the folders macOS protects (Mail, Messages, Safari).
settings.disk-access.missing.desc: Without it, macOS hides Mail, Messages and Safari from POSMA. It can only be granted in System Settings: tick POSMA there and this row notices by itself.
settings.system.desc: {summary}. A change below reaches every module.
settings.blacklist.desc: Paths the scanners never list or offer to delete — another system's drive, a photo archive, a client's documents.
settings.blacklist.pick: Choose a folder the scanners must never show
settings.refresh.desc: How often live views ask for new data. Less often means less work in the background; charts stay smooth either way.
settings.reminders.desc: Quiet notifications when cleaning is due (for example, a disk over 85% full).
settings.language.desc: The language of the app's interface.
settings.reset.desc: Removes the app with all its modules, settings and data. For now it resets the app's state (setup starts over).
settings.reset.confirm: Are you sure? This clears the app's state and starts setup over.
view.vault.loading.title: Starting the vault
view.vault.loading.note: Opening the encrypted database and getting it ready to unlock.
view.vault.unlock.key-missing: The PIN is correct, but the vault key is no longer in the system keystore (KWallet, GNOME Keyring, Keychain, Credential Manager). This can happen after reinstalling the system. Without the key the saved passwords cannot be read. If you have a copy of the old keystore, restore it; if not, you can start a new vault.
view.vault.unlock.confirm-reset: Delete the old vault and create a new one? The passwords saved in it cannot be recovered.
view.vault.pin-length: The PIN must be exactly 6 digits.
view.vault.unlock.locked-out: Too many attempts. Try again in {n} s.
view.vault.create.title: Create a password vault
view.vault.unlock.title: Unlock the vault
view.vault.create.note: The real encryption key is generated at random and kept in the system keystore (Secret Service / Keychain), never in the vault file. The 6-digit PIN is only a quick access lock, not the key.
view.vault.unlock.note: Enter your 6-digit PIN to unlock the vault.
view.vault.unlock.start-over: Delete the old vault and create a new one
view.vault.generator.title: Password generator
view.vault.entry.title-required: Enter a title for the entry.
view.vault.entry.title: Title
view.vault.detail.confirm-delete: Delete this entry? This cannot be undone.
view.vault.change-pin.mismatch: The new PINs do not match.
view.vault.change-pin.title: Change PIN
view.vault.change-pin.done: PIN changed. The encryption key stayed the same, so nothing had to be re-encrypted.
view.vault.audit.title: Security audit
view.vault.audit.none: No weak or reused passwords found.
view.vault.heading: Vault

view.duplicates.confirm.one: Delete {n} file ({size}) and keep the copies you ticked in each group? This cannot be undone.
view.duplicates.confirm.other: Delete {n} files ({size}) and keep the copies you ticked in each group? This cannot be undone.

view.duplicates.confirm-versions.one: Delete {n} older version ({size}) and keep the versions you ticked in each group? This cannot be undone.
view.duplicates.confirm-versions.other: Delete {n} older versions ({size}) and keep the versions you ticked in each group? This cannot be undone.

view.duplicates.intro: Search Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Desktop, Videos and Music for identical files (SHA-256). Developer tool folders (node_modules, build, .git...) are skipped.
view.duplicates.none: No duplicates in the folders searched.
view.duplicates.versions.heading: Old versions of the same file or folder
view.duplicates.versions.intro: Find files and folders whose names differ only by a version number (for example AppName_2.2.zip next to AppName_2.5.zip). That usually means a leftover old copy.
view.duplicates.versions.none: No names that differ only by version found.
view.shredder.warning.title: This cannot be undone.
view.shredder.warning.body: The files and folders you choose are overwritten with random data ({passes}×), renamed and deleted. You cannot get them back from the Trash or undo it.
view.shredder.heading: To shred
view.metadata.intro.title: Hidden data in photos
view.metadata.intro.body: Photos from phones and cameras often carry EXIF data (device model, date, sometimes the exact GPS location) and text comments or tags. Choose JPEG or PNG files, expand an item to see exactly what is in it, and pick what to remove. You can keep the rest, such as the date the photo was taken.
view.metadata.heading: To check
view.metadata.keep-hint: Tick what to keep. The rest is removed when you clean.

view.temp-clean.confirm.one: Delete {n} item ({size})? This cannot be undone.
view.temp-clean.confirm.other: Delete {n} items ({size})? This cannot be undone.

view.temp-clean.intro: Scan the known temporary file locations. Nothing is deleted without your confirmation.

view.big-files.confirm.one: Delete {n} file ({size})? This cannot be undone.
view.big-files.confirm.other: Delete {n} files ({size})? This cannot be undone.

view.big-files.intro: Search your home folder for files larger than {mb} MB, from installers to forgotten virtual machine images. The .git folder is skipped.
view.big-files.none: No files larger than {mb} MB found.
view.big-files.heading: Largest files
view.journald-trim.confirm.size: Trim the system logs (down to {amount})? Deleted journal entries do not come back. This does not touch apps or their data, only the systemd log history.
view.journald-trim.confirm.time: Trim the system logs (older than {amount})? Deleted journal entries do not come back. This does not touch apps or their data, only the systemd log history.
view.boot-loader.hint.limine.default: Path of an entry from the list (e.g. CachyOS/linux-cachyos) or its number, counting from 1. If the file sets remember_last_entry: yes, Limine prefers the entry that ran last.
view.boot-loader.hint.limine.timeout: Seconds; "no" waits for a choice, 0 skips the menu.
view.boot-loader.hint.systemd-boot.defau: ID of an entry from the list (e.g. arch.conf), a pattern with * or @saved for the last one chosen. An entry set in the menu itself with the d key takes precedence.
view.boot-loader.hint.systemd-boot.timeo: Seconds; menu-force waits for a choice, menu-hidden shows the menu only when a key is pressed.
view.boot-loader.hint.refind.default: Part of an entry name or its number from 1. rEFInd finds most systems on its own at startup, so the list only has entries written in refind.conf.
view.boot-loader.hint.refind.timeout: Seconds; 0 waits for a choice, -1 boots right away.
view.boot-loader.error.not-this-loader: As an administrator, this system does not look like it boots with {name} — check "Boot loader" in settings.
view.boot-loader.save.confirm: Save the {name} settings? The previous configuration is kept as a backup.
view.boot-loader.restore.confirm: Restore this backup? The current configuration is saved as a backup too.
view.boot-loader.title: Boot: {name}
view.boot-loader.intro: {name} reads its configuration from the boot partition, which only an administrator can read — so even viewing the settings asks for permission.
view.boot-loader.empty-keeps: An empty field leaves the setting unchanged.
view.boot-loader.saved: Saved — the change takes effect at the next boot.
view.boot-loader.backups.empty: No backups — they appear after the first save.
view.kernel-mgr.remove.confirm: Remove kernel {version} ({size})? This cannot be undone. The running and the latest kernel are always protected, but make sure you do not need this one.
view.kernel-mgr.preparing.title: Checking installed kernels
view.kernel-mgr.preparing.note: Finding which kernel is running and which is the latest — both are locked against removal.
view.kernel-mgr.nothing-to-remove: Nothing to remove here — only the running and the latest kernel are left.
view.time-machine.remove.confirm-keep: Remove all local Time Machine snapshots except the newest?
view.time-machine.remove.confirm-all: Remove all local Time Machine snapshots? Backups on the backup disk stay, but until the next backup you cannot go back to a state before it from this Mac.
view.time-machine.preparing.title: Checking Time Machine snapshots
view.time-machine.preparing.note: Asking tmutil for the local snapshots of the startup disk.

view.time-machine.count.one: local snapshot on the startup disk
view.time-machine.count.other: local snapshots on the startup disk

view.time-machine.empty: No local snapshots — nothing here takes up space.
view.pkg-cache.clean.rollback: This also removes the previous versions you could roll back to after a failed update.
view.pkg-cache.clean.confirm: Remove {size} of {manager} cache? Downloaded packages will be fetched again when needed.

view.pkg-cache.snaps.confirm.one: Remove {n} old snap revision? This cannot be undone.
view.pkg-cache.snaps.confirm.other: Remove {n} old snap revisions? This cannot be undone.

view.pkg-cache.preparing.title: Counting what can be recovered
view.pkg-cache.preparing.note: Checking the downloaded package cache, orphaned packages and old snap revisions.
view.xcode-cache.xcode.scanning-note: Measuring the build and device symbol folders. This takes a moment with large projects.
view.xcode-cache.xcode.absent: No Xcode folder found — this module has nothing to clean here.
view.xcode-cache.macos-slim.scanning-not: Measuring copies of opened attachments, previews and cache. Your messages and conversations are not even read.
view.xcode-cache.macos-slim.absent: Mail and Messages have not been used on this Mac — there is nothing to slim down.
view.xcode-cache.macos-slim.summary: taken up by Mail and Messages copies and cache
view.xcode-cache.blocked: macOS did not show: {list}. Without Full Disk Access these places are closed to POSMA.
view.grub-editor.save.confirm: Save the GRUB settings? A backup of the previous configuration is made and grub.cfg is regenerated.
view.grub-editor.theme.pick-title: Choose the folder with the unpacked GRUB theme
view.grub-editor.theme.install.confirm: Install and enable the theme "{name}"? It is copied to {dir} and set as active.
view.grub-editor.theme.disable.confirm: Disable the theme and go back to the default GRUB look? The theme files stay on disk.
view.grub-editor.presets.prompt: Preset name (saves the current settings from the form):
view.grub-editor.presets.apply.confirm: Apply the preset "{name}"? It overwrites the current GRUB settings (with a backup).
view.grub-editor.restore.confirm: Restore this backup? The current configuration is saved as a backup before restoring.
view.grub-editor.preparing.title: Loading the boot configuration
view.grub-editor.preparing.note: Reading the boot settings and the list of saved backups.
view.grub-editor.os-prober: Turn off detection of other systems (os-prober)
view.grub-editor.theme.invalid: This does not look like a GRUB theme — there is no theme.txt in the chosen folder.
view.grub-editor.theme.name: Name (target folder in {dir})
view.grub-editor.backups.keep-note: 2 by default — older backups are removed automatically on the next save
view.grub-editor.backups.empty: No backups — they appear after the first save.
view.desktop-theme.install.pick-title: Choose a folder with a theme, icon set or cursor
view.desktop-theme.presets.apply.confirm: Apply the set "{name}"? It changes the current look of the desktop.
view.desktop-theme.read-failed: Could not read the desktop settings.
view.desktop-theme.locked-note: You can still install themes and fonts — changing settings is unavailable.
view.desktop-theme.plasma-note: Reading KDE Plasma settings was tested on Plasma 6, writing was not yet. Report it if something does not work here.
view.desktop-theme.install.note: Detects on its own whether the folder is a GTK theme, an icon set or a cursor, and copies it to your home folder.
view.desktop-theme.install.theme: Install a theme from a folder
view.desktop-theme.install.font: Install a font from a file
view.desktop-theme.presets.note: Saves the current look under a name so you can return to it with one click.

view.uninstaller.apps.loading.note: Asking the system package manager, snap and flatpak in turn. Each answers at its own pace.

view.uninstaller.scan.confirm.one: Remove {n} item ({size})? This cannot be undone.
view.uninstaller.scan.confirm.other: Remove {n} items ({size})? This cannot be undone.

view.uninstaller.scan.intro.after: for folders that match no installed program. This is a heuristic: plugins and AppImages may show up even though they are in use, so check before you delete.
view.uninstaller.scan.loading.title: Looking for leftovers
view.uninstaller.scan.loading.note: Going through config, cache and data folders for traces of uninstalled programs.
view.autostart.form.required: Enter a name and a path.
view.autostart.delete.confirm: Delete the entry "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
view.autostart.intro: Review the programs that start automatically when you log in (~/.config/autostart) and turn off the ones you do not need. Nothing is deleted, so you can always turn them back on.
view.autostart.title: Startup programs

view.autostart.form.not-found: No file found at this path.
view.autostart.form.not-executable: This file is not executable, so the entry will not start at login.

view.health-monitor.loading.note: Collecting temperatures, load and drive health. The first reading takes longer than the next ones.
view.health-monitor.kill.confirm: End the process "{name}" (PID {pid})? Unsaved data in it will be lost.
view.health-monitor.sensors.title: Sensors
view.health-monitor.top.title: Heaviest processes
view.health-monitor.top.cpu-hint: Sum over all cores: 150% is one and a half cores
view.disk-map.intro.title: What takes up space
view.disk-map.intro.body: A folder, layer by layer, with the largest items on top. Click a folder to go deeper, or pick another starting point below. The ⋯ button (or a right click) shows an item in the file manager or deletes it, permanently and only after you confirm.
view.disk-map.loading.title: Preparing the disk map
view.disk-map.loading.note: Going through every folder and adding up sizes. There is no other way to show what really takes up space.
view.services.restore.confirm: Restore the default settings of the "{name}" services? A system restore point is created first.
view.services.disable.confirm: Turn off the "{name}" services? {effect} A system restore point is created first, and Windows asks for administrator approval once.
view.services.loading.title: Checking services
view.services.loading.note: Asking Windows about the services in the ready-made profiles.
view.services.empty: This edition of Windows has none of the services the profiles cover.
view.winget.loading.title: Checking for updates

view.winsxs.clean.confirm: Remove the superseded versions of Windows components? A restore point is created first. Cleaning usually takes ten minutes or so, and installed updates cannot be uninstalled afterwards.
view.winsxs.title: Component store
view.winsxs.desc: Old versions of system files that Windows keeps after updates. Check first whether cleaning is recommended.

view.browser-hygiene.none: No supported browsers found (Firefox, Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge, Opera, Vivaldi).

dashboard.cpu.error: Could not read the machine's state — the system-info module is not responding.
dashboard.cpu.wait: The line needs two readings — waiting for the next one…
dashboard.caption.b: , the dashed one is the busiest core; the scale adapts to the load. The bars are the cores right now, 0–100%. Hover a bar to see that core's history;
dashboard.caption.c: (or press Enter) to watch it permanently, several at once if you like.
dashboard.crowded: Disk almost full — the disk map shows what takes up the space ({code})
dashboard.reclaim.note: Read-only. You delete inside a module, after it asks you to confirm.
dashboard.reclaim.none: No enabled module frees disk space.

appearance.accent.custom.label: Custom accent colour
appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.mode.desc: Every look has a light and a dark version. System follows the system setting.
appearance.accent.weak: This colour barely stands out from the background ({ratio}:1) — selections and outlines may vanish.
appearance.accent.desc: The colour of buttons, selections and the focus outline. Preset colours have a separate shade for light and dark backgrounds.
appearance.contrast.desc: High brings descriptions, captions and lines closer to the text colour.
appearance.font.desc: Atkinson Hyperlegible tells apart letters other typefaces blur together (Il1, O0).
appearance.numfont.desc: Readings, paths and catalogue numbers. Digits always have equal width.
appearance.labels.desc: Section captions, buttons and folder names.
appearance.scale.desc.auto: Automatic picks the scale from the window size — now {pct}%.
appearance.scale.desc.manual: Set it by hand if the text is too small or too large at your resolution.
appearance.lines.desc: Thickness of borders, dividers and chart lines.
appearance.density.desc: Spacing in lists, tables and the sidebar.
appearance.motion.desc: Reduced keeps fades but nothing moves. Off turns every animation off.
appearance.grid.desc: Horizontal scale lines under the CPU profile.
appearance.peak.desc: The busiest core, drawn next to the average.
appearance.reset.desc: Undoes accent, contrast, typefaces, labels, corners, lines, density and chart. Mode, scale and motion stay.
appearance.reset.none: Nothing is overridden — you see the look as it is.
world-info.katalog.desc: Catalogue numbers, a folder bar, the CPU profile. Comes in five variants.
world-info.gesto.desc: Everything on one screen: a mosaic of modules with red tabs.
world-info.kaseta.desc: The disk as a tape: a shelf of cassettes, an insert with side A and B.
world-info.strumien.desc: One thing per screen, the next one a scroll away.
world-info.ksiazeczka.desc: Free space as a balance, every operation a stamped entry.
world-info.monochrom.desc: One grey scale: every sentence with its evidence beside it.
look.katalog.desc: Matte black, wide capitals, catalogue numbers.
look.systemowy.desc: The system typeface, cards and rounded corners, like a native app.
look.plakat.desc: Swiss style: heavy dividers, huge numbers, red.
look.konsola.desc: All monospace, terminal colours, frames like in btop.
look.kalkulator.desc: Graphite and round keys, the number in a display window.
folder-view.empty: This folder has no modules for your system yet.
folder-view.disable.title: Hide this module — files stay on disk
module-view.placeholder.1: The interface of the “{name}” module will arrive in later stages —
module-view.placeholder.2: this is where its scanning, preview and action UI will go.
onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to POSMA
onboarding.welcome.lead: POSMA is a modular system caretaker: cleaning, monitoring, autostart, security. Before we begin, we need your consent for the app to run and to carry out operations on this computer. Every risky action always asks for its own confirmation.
onboarding.os.title: Confirm your system
onboarding.os.lead.linux: We detected your distribution. It decides how modules work: package commands, desktop look, boot. Is this your system?
onboarding.os.lead.other: We detected your operating system. It decides which modules are available.
onboarding.os.sub.other: General modules + modules available only for {os}
onboarding.access.title: Access level
onboarding.access.lead: You can change this later in settings.
onboarding.access.full.title: Full
onboarding.access.full.desc: The app collects access to every possible feature right away, whether or not the module is installed.
onboarding.access.full.fine: Goal: as few restarts and prompts as possible. Effect: no restarts when you add modules later.
onboarding.access.selective.title: Selective
onboarding.access.selective.desc: The app asks only for the access the modules you actually choose need.
onboarding.access.selective.fine: Effect: the app or system may need a restart when you add more modules.
onboarding.modules.title: Choose modules
onboarding.modules.lead: We will install only what you tick. You can add the rest later in module management.
onboarding.tutorial.title: Almost done
onboarding.tutorial.lead: Want a tour of the app? A dozen short steps, about two minutes. You can come back to it any time under 904 in the sidebar.
preparing.timer: running for {n} s: this is normal with larger disks
missing.hint: Installing packages needs administrator rights. This feature will arrive with the permission broker (Access_plan.md). For now, run this command yourself.
profile.family.declared: It is set by /etc/os-release ({source}) and the installed {family}. Administrator operations pick it the same way, so it is not changed here.
profile.family.undeclared: The system does not declare a family. Choose which of the installed package managers it uses.
profile.family.name: System family
profile.desktop.name: Desktop environment
profile.desktop.desc: It decides how the appearance module changes themes, icons, cursors and fonts.
profile.bootloader.name: Boot loader
profile.bootloader.desc: It decides which boot editor opens: GRUB, Limine, systemd-boot or rEFInd.
cpu.heading: cores now · 0–100%
cpu.aria: Processor over the last {span}: mean {mean}, busiest core {peak}. {watching}Arrow keys pick a core and show its history, Enter watches it.
tour.keys: Arrow keys move between steps, Esc ends the tour
tour.module.hero.title: Module
tour.module.hero.text: The header says what the module does and how risky it is: Safe, Careful or Critical. The higher the risk, the more questions before a change.
tour.module.flow.title: Scan, review, confirm
tour.module.flow.text: A module only reads at first. You get a list with sizes, you pick the items, and nothing goes until you confirm.
tour.cpu.title: Processor gauge
tour.cpu.text.katalog: The line is the mean of the whole processor, the dashed one is the busiest core. The bars are each core right now. Click a bar and that core stays on the chart.
tour.cpu.text.other: Live processor load: the mean of all cores and the busiest core. The reading refreshes by itself.
tour.machine.title: This machine
tour.machine.text.katalog: System, disks, memory and temperature in one table. A value in the warning colour is worth your attention, and a shortcut to the right module sits right below it.
tour.machine.text.other: System, disks, memory and temperature. A value marked as a warning is worth your attention.
tour.reclaim.title: How much you can reclaim
tour.reclaim.text: One button asks every enabled module how much space it would free. It only reads: you always delete inside a module, after its confirmation.
tour.index.title: Index
tour.index.text.katalog: The main actions of enabled modules in one list, with the catalog number and a reading beside each. The coloured bar shows which folder they come from.
tour.index.text.other: The main actions of enabled modules gathered in one place. Each leads to its module.
tour.numbers.title: Catalog numbers
tour.numbers.text: The hundreds are folders: 100 data and files, 200 system, 300 security, 400 apps, 500 custom. Every module has its own number, and 900 is the app itself.
tour.folder.title: Folder
tour.folder.text.katalog: Each row is a module: number, description, risk level and one main action. Drag a row to reorder, and the sidebar follows.
tour.folder.text.other: The modules in this folder: number, description, risk level and one main action.
tour.security.title: Security
tour.security.text: Browser hygiene clears cache, cookies and history. Vault is a local, encrypted password store with a security audit.
tour.manager.title: Module management
tour.manager.text.katalog: Enable only what you need. A disabled module disappears from the sidebar and the index, and its catalog number stays.
tour.manager.text.other: Enable only what you need. A disabled module disappears from the navigation and the dashboard, and its catalog number stays.
tour.access.title: Access level
tour.access.text: Full collects every consent up front and remembers it. Selective grants permissions for one run and asks again after a restart.
tour.blacklist.title: Blocklist
tour.blacklist.text: Paths no scanner will list or suggest for removal: another system’s disk, a photo archive, a client’s documents.
tour.look.title: Appearance
tour.look.text: Six worlds, each with its own navigation and dashboard, light and dark; Catalog has five more variants. Below you can override accent, contrast, typeface, labels, corners, density, motion and chart. One button returns to the world’s settings.
tour.return.title: The tour stays here
tour.return.text: You can come back to it any time under 904. That is the end of the tour.
